title: GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades 500s on a legacy/out-of-taxonomy exit_reason value
description: `GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades` returns a bare 500 (unhandled `pydantic_core.ValidationError`) when any row in the `closed_trades` table has an `exit_reason` string that isn't one of the 8 `ExitReasonOut` Literal values (`target_hit`, `stop_hit`, `reached_value_zone`, `going_nowhere`, `starting_to_turn`, `couldnt_stand_the_pain`, `recognized_junk_trade_after_entry`, `unspecified`). Observed in a dev environment with a row whose `exit_reason` is `'manual'` -- not a value this app's own code ever writes (DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id}'s `exit_reason` query param is itself an `ExitReason` enum with no 'manual' member; grep confirms 'manual' only appears elsewhere as an unrelated `trade_apgar.py` 'source' literal), so it's most likely hand-inserted dev/seed data or a leftover from a schema/taxonomy version predating the current `ExitReason` enum -- but the underlying bug is real regardless of how that row got there. Root cause: `backend/app/db/models.py` stores `ClosedTradeORM.exit_reason` as a plain unconstrained `String` column (no DB-level check constraint), while `_to_closed_trade_out` in `backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py` (line ~235) does `exit_reason=cast(ExitReasonOut, row.exit_reason)` -- a type-checker-only `cast`, not a runtime validation/coercion -- so any row with a value outside the Literal blows up the whole list endpoint for every trade, not just the offending row, via a Python list comprehension with no per-row error isolation (`ClosedTradesResponse(items=[_to_closed_trade_out(row, grades[row.id]) for row in rows])`, line ~891). This violates the app's general degrade-gracefully contract (seen elsewhere e.g. IBKR-unavailable handling, malformed-daily-bar filtering) -- one bad row shouldn't take down the whole trade history/journal view.

checklist.step: Decide and record (a decisions entry) how to handle a row whose exit_reason falls outside the ExitReasonOut taxonomy: e.g. map it to 'unspecified' at the API boundary (in _to_closed_trade_out, replacing the blind cast with an actual validation/fallback), vs. widening the ExitReasonOut Literal/ExitReason enum to add a value, vs. some other approach -- weigh against what the value likely means (a genuine data-entry/legacy value vs. real taxonomy gap).
Implement the chosen fix in _to_closed_trade_out (and record_follow_up_review's shared call site) so an out-of-taxonomy exit_reason value degrades gracefully instead of 500ing the whole list.

Decide whether this should also isolate a single bad row's failure from the rest of the response (so one malformed row can't ever again take down every other trade in the list), independent of the exit_reason-specific fix.
Unit/integration test: a closed_trades row with an out-of-taxonomy exit_reason value (e.g. 'manual') no longer 500s GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades, and the response's other rows are unaffected.
If the taxonomy itself changes (a new ExitReasonOut value added), regenerate backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts.

decisions.decision: An out-of-taxonomy `exit_reason` value read from the `closed_trades` table (e.g. 'manual') is normalized to `'unspecified'` at the API boundary in `_to_closed_trade_out` (new `_normalize_exit_reason` helper, checked against `get_args(ExitReasonOut)`), replacing the type-checker-only `cast(ExitReasonOut, row.exit_reason)`. Widening the `ExitReasonOut` Literal / `ExitReason` enum to add a `'manual'` member (or similar) was considered and rejected: `'manual'` is not a value any current code path writes (DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id}'s own `exit_reason` query param is itself the `ExitReason` enum with no such member), so it reads as stale/hand-inserted dev data or a leftover from a taxonomy version that predates the current 8-value `ExitReason` enum, not a genuine gap in Elder's own exit-reason taxonomy (docs/Analyse.md §7) that the app needs to represent going forward. `'unspecified'` is already this app's own established sentinel for 'no real reason known' (see `app.portfolio.models.ExitReason.UNSPECIFIED`'s own docstring, used for the exact same 'don't actually know why' situation when DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id} is called with no `exit_reason` supplied), so reusing it here needs no schema change and keeps the taxonomy's meaning stable for every future caller. The out-of-taxonomy value is still logged (`logger.warning`) so it isn't silently lost -- only the API response coerces it.
decisions.rationale: Widening the taxonomy would permanently validate what's most likely bad/legacy data as a first-class, book-derived exit reason, and would require a schema change (openapi.json + frontend types) for a value with no evidence of being a real, ongoing use case. A fallback needs no schema change, degrades gracefully exactly like this app's other data-quality issues (IBKR-unavailable handling, malformed-daily-bar filtering), and is trivially reversible if a genuine new taxonomy value is ever needed later.

decisions.decision: Beyond the exit_reason-specific fix, `get_closed_trades` also isolates each row's `_to_closed_trade_out` call in its own try/except inside the loop that builds `ClosedTradesResponse.items`: a row that still fails for any other, unanticipated reason is dropped from the response and logged (`logger.exception`) rather than 500ing every other trade in the list. `record_follow_up_review` (the single-row POST endpoint) is left as-is, without an equivalent try/except -- there is no 'other row' to isolate a failure from there, and the caller explicitly asked to act on that one `trade_id`, so surfacing a genuine failure for it (rather than silently swallowing it) is the more useful behavior for that endpoint.
decisions.rationale: The exit_reason fallback alone fixes the one failure mode actually observed, but the task explicitly asks to consider isolation independent of that fix, and the app's own degrade-gracefully convention (grading failures, malformed-daily-bar filtering) already treats 'one bad row breaks the whole list' as a bug class, not just specific to exit_reason. A narrow try/except around the one per-row call site is the minimal way to extend that convention here without swallowing errors more broadly (e.g. wrapping the whole endpoint) that could mask a real, systemic bug instead of an isolated bad row.

decisions.decision: No `ExitReasonOut` taxonomy change was made (fallback-to-'unspecified' approach, see above), so regenerating `backend/openapi.json`/`frontend/src/api/types.ts` is a no-op for this task -- confirmed by running `python scripts/export_openapi.py` and diffing against the committed snapshot (no changes) rather than skipping the check.
decisions.rationale: Checklist item 5 is conditional on widening the taxonomy; recording explicitly that the condition wasn't met (and that this was verified, not assumed) avoids the next reader wondering whether the snapshot was simply forgotten.

comments.summary: Non-blocking: get_closed_trades's per-row `except Exception` around _to_closed_trade_out is intentionally broad (narrower than wrapping the whole endpoint, per the task's own decisions entry), but that breadth means a future systemic bug affecting every row would degrade to a silently near-/fully-empty 200 in production, visible only via a per-row logger.exception line rather than any aggregate signal. Worth a per-request dropped-row count/metric or aggregate log line later. Tracked on backend-closed-trades-legacy-exit-reason-500-followups.

Non-blocking: _normalize_exit_reason's logger.warning fires on every request that includes a persistent out-of-taxonomy row, not just once -- could produce repeated identical log noise for a long-lived legacy row. Likely acceptable (matches existing per-request logging conventions elsewhere) but worth reconsidering. Tracked on backend-closed-trades-legacy-exit-reason-500-followups.
